items.title: Chuck Findley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 6, 2023
items.q: I’d come home for lunch and Seely would have lunch with me.

ctx.x: Yeah I really didn’t do much of that. I would just record for them and then they would get bands and musicians to take on the road. You know I just did the records. I really didn’t, I was so busy I was enjoying going home for lunch, you know I lived in Studio City and I’d be at Universal and I’d come home for lunch and Seely would have lunch with me. Or dinner. I lived close. I always wanted to be close. And I would tell musicians too that first moved to town, I said if you want to be close, you need to be close…

you get a last minute call, somebody can’t make it or their car broke down or they got — whatever, something happened, and we need somebody right away, you get a phone call and we need you right away you know. Can you get there in like 20 minutes or something like that. And so back in those days you could. If you lived in North Hollywood, Studio City, anywhere like that, everything was in Hollywood pretty much or Burbank. Pretty much Hollywood, the studios are in Hollywood. And they could be there in 15 minutes,…
